questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches you.
Keep driving but move out of its way.
Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must give the right-of-way to all emergency vehicles with sirens and flashing lights. Pull to the right edge of the road when possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first before pulling over.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line on your side means you cannot pass other vehicles from your direction.

questions.question: What is a good way to reduce tiredness on a long drive?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours for a short break to avoid getting tired. If you become drowsy, pull off the road to a safe place and take a nap or rest for the night.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, what should you expect?

options.text: They will know when it is safe to cross the street.
They will stop at the curb before crossing.
They may run in front of you without looking.
They will not cross unless an adult is with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may run in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful when children are nearby. Children may not understand danger and may run into the street without looking first.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After you finish the turn, where should your car be?

options.text: In the right lane of the street.
In the center of the street.
In the left lane of the street.
In the lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the left lane of the street.
questions.explanation: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, finish the turn in the lane closest to where you came from.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that two lanes of traffic moving in the same direction will soon become one lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic light is coming. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: Why does night driving require extra caution?

options.text: There is more traffic at night.
Drivers cannot see as well at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers cannot see as well at night.
questions.explanation: Darkness makes it harder to see. Use your headlights from 30 minutes after sunset until 30 minutes before sunrise, or whenever you cannot see 500 feet ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. They prepare you for road conditions ahead. This sign tells you that a new lane is being added.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulation signs show traffic rules you must follow. This sign means vehicles in the left lane must turn left.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if there are no other cars.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.

questions.explanation: A steady red light means you must stop completely. Driving through a red light is illegal and dangerous. You may turn right on red only if a sign does not forbid it.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on major highways?

options.text: Be ready to react to road hazards.

questions.explanation: Always stay alert on highways and be ready for unexpected hazards. Keep your eyes moving and avoid looking at one thing for too long to prevent highway hypnosis.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing with no warning lights or gates?

options.text: Cross quickly as fast as you can.
Always come to a complete stop.
Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to beat any oncoming train.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to trains at railroad crossings, especially when there are no lights or gates. Do not cross until your entire vehicle can fit on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing because your vehicle could stall.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle when:

options.text: You see a stop sign at an intersection.
A red light is on or flashing.
A traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop at stop signs, at red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: How much space you need to cross traffic depends on:

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
Whether there is a stop sign.
Whether you use your turn signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: How can you help prevent crashes?

options.text: Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do something others do not expect. Communicate with other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by signaling when you slow down, stop, or change direction. Use your horn or emergency signals when needed.

questions.question: Drivers who eat or drink while driving:

options.text: Are better drivers because they are not hungry.

questions.explanation: Eating, drinking, or smoking while driving is dangerous because it requires you to take your hands off the wheel and eyes off the road. This makes it harder to stay in your lane and control your vehicle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers which direction they must drive on a one-way street. It is a regulation sign that controls traffic movement.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns you of a hazard. Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.question: A driver ahead is driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Recognize that the driver is distracted and less safe.
Do not follow the driver's example.

questions.explanation: Do not become distracted by passengers, searching your vehicle, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming. If a driver near you seems distracted, give them extra space because the risk of a crash is higher.

questions.question: Where should you keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.

questions.explanation: Keep space around all sides of your vehicle. This gives you time to react to dangers. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left or right.

questions.question: When turning left, you must yield to:
questions.explanation: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers who are already in the intersection.

questions.question: On a freeway, if you miss your exit, you should:

options.text: Keep driving until the next exit where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop for you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until the next exit where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: Do not back up on a freeway. Go to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: To be ready for what is ahead on the road, you should:

options.text: Look at the whole road and both sides.
Rest your left foot on the brake pedal.
Focus on the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the whole road and both sides.
questions.explanation: Look for problems early. Scan the entire road and both sides, not just straight ahead. This helps you handle dangerous situations.

questions.question: When facing bright headlights from another car, you should:

options.text: Use your bright lights until they dim theirs.
Flash your lights to warn them.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road, not at the bright headlights. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: To change lanes, you should:

options.text: Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
Signal, check mirrors, then change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check mirrors, check your blind spot, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn on your signal. Check your mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Make sure no one is in the lane you want to enter. Then change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, you should:

options.text: Speed up as fast as you can.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.explanation: A green light means you can go. But first, let pedestrians and other traffic clear the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a roundabout is coming. Enter it slowly and yield to traffic already inside.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign is posted at traffic lights where you cannot turn right on red.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn here.
